## Summary

Extends the merged MavebBench foundation with two real-data capabilities rather than status-only placeholders:

- converts raw ARKitScenes low-resolution RGB/depth/confidence/intrinsics/trajectory data into the exact MavebCapture schema-v2 contract consumed by `RecordedSequenceSource`
- validates converted ARKitScenes packages through the real `aether-fuse --dry-run` reader/fusion contract
- adds ETH3D metric geometry evaluation against `dslr_scan_eval/scan1.ply`
- aligns arbitrary-scale COLMAP reconstructions to ETH3D's calibrated camera frame using an explicit camera-centre Umeyama Sim(3), then reports accuracy/completeness/Chamfer/p95 and F-scores at 1/2/5 cm
- records the alignment method/matrix and can export the aligned candidate point cloud
- updates manifests, docs, README and benchmark reporting
- adds ARKit pose/depth synchronization tests and geometry-alignment/metric tests

## Local validation

- Python compile check passed for the benchmark, ARKit adapter and geometry evaluator
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s benchmarks/tests -p 'test_*.py'` — 15/15 tests pass
- manifest JSON validation passed
- remote tree readback verified after commit

## Truthfulness / remaining gates

This does not claim the dense CPU TSDF is a room-scale production fusion backend. ARKitScenes is converted and contract-validated; publishing ARKitScenes fusion/accuracy numbers still requires running the committed adapter against the downloaded local scene. DTU keeps an explicit benchmark-specific adapter gate. Dense RGB geometry, adaptive video keyframes, Blender-ready GLB export, sparse Metal TSDF, residual appearance, `.aether` v2 rate-distortion/LOD and Vulkan remain separate roadmap work.

## What this is

The root README described the repo as it stood when the AI-GM tabletop game *was* the repo. Everything built since — the Circuit, the tactical prototypes, the witness worker, the art direction, the diorama vision — was invisible from the front door.

## The reframe

The repo is a **universe** (post-collapse North America, eleven factions, competing truths) and every game being built inside it. The README now opens with that, and names the through-line honestly: the Witnesses' motto — *"we remember so you don't have to lie"* — is faction lore in the fiction and engineering doctrine in the code. Golden transcripts, replay-verified match records, and a content-addressed archive are that motto, implemented.

## Structure

- **Status table up top**, honest per design philosophy: tabletop **Playable** (450+ tests), Circuit **Playable prototype**, Witness **Live** on Workers, world game **Direction — pieces prototyped**. Nothing claims to be more finished than it is.

## Accuracy notes

items.title: docs: republish accuracy from the corrected estimator, and retire a claim
items.body:
Two training runs have landed since [#404](https://github.com/kristenmartino/gridpulse/pull/404) fixed ledger-23, so the published accuracy numbers can be **replaced with measured ones** instead of carrying a warning that they are wrong.

Regenerated from production GCS metas at `latest.json`, 2026-08-07, all 51 regions — **all 51 reporting `scored="out_of_sample"`**.

| Statistic | XGBoost-only | Best-base per BA | Ensemble (served) |
|---|---|---|---|
| min | 1.89% (ERCOT) | 1.72% (ERCOT) | 1.38% (SPP) |
| median | 3.69% | 3.69% | **4.35%** |
| mean | 5.37% | 4.95% | **6.27%** |
| p90 | 9.87% | 9.87% | **14.27%** |
| max | 37.50% (SPA) | 23.26% (SPA) | **30.86%** (IID) |

## Two changes moved this table, and they are separable

The base columns come from `_holdout_metrics_*`, which ledger-23 **never touched** — they moved purely from a month of retraining. Only the ensemble column carries the bias correction, and it was measured on the *same* run with the old estimator logged beside the new:

| ensemble median | |
|---|---|
| previously published (2026-07-03, in-sample) | 4.82% |
| 2026-08-07, in-sample — what the old code would say today | 3.89% |
| **2026-08-07, out-of-sample — published** | **4.35%** |

Retraining bought **−0.93 pts**; the correction gave back **+0.46**. Both are in the docs; neither is presented as the whole story.

The correction is **far larger in the tail than at the median** — mean +1.32 against median +0.46, worse on 33 of 51 BAs. That is the shape you would expect: in-sample weighting has most to exploit where models disagree most.

## A claim is withdrawn, not restated

Both docs argued the ensemble earns its keep as *variance-reduction on the tail*, resting on **SEC 38.63% → 13.61%**. On 2026-08-07 SEC is XGBoost **13.68%** and ensemble **14.72%** — the blend is *worse* there. Ensemble p90 (14.27%) is now well above XGBoost-only’s (9.87%).

I did not hunt for a replacement example. A claim that needs a freshly-chosen example every retrain was never a claim. The honest statement is that the blend buys error decorrelation on some BAs and costs accuracy on others, and only the per-BA table says which.

## Consequences of the same table, also corrected

- Best base is XGBoost on **42 of 51**, not 44 — and **which model wins a BA is not stable across retrains**: only SEC and SC held their column since July. Called out explicitly, because citing a BA’s champion from memory is now a trap.
- Ensemble beats XGBoost-alone on **21 of 51**, not 17 (`HOW_IT_WORKS`, `INTERVIEW_PREP`, `README`).
- README’s XGBoost line: 42 of 51, ERCOT 1.89%, median 3.69%.
- The 51-row per-BA table in `BACKTEST_RESULTS` regenerated from the same pull.

## Notes

`docs/_holdout_table.md` was regenerated locally and matches `BACKTEST_RESULTS` **row-for-row on all 51 BAs (0 mismatches, verified)** — but is **not in this commit**: it is gitignored as a regenerable artifact, which is right for a file that goes stale every training run.

Five references to `2026-07-03` survive on purpose — each is explicitly the older measurement being compared against, not a live figure.

## Explanatory-doc check

- Architecture changed? No.
- Cited fact moved? **Yes** — `CANONICAL_FACTS` accuracy block updated here, in the same commit as its consumers.
- STAR-story trigger? The arc belongs at #273 close.
- `STATUS.md`? No change to active focus.

Docs-only.

Refs #273

items.title: Add tests for regression and global pruning, and make CCL failures fail CI
items.body:
Adds tests for univariate regression and Global Pruning, neither of which had any.

## Why these two

A coverage measurement — profiling every exported function while running the paths the suite exercises — found that of 49 exported symbols, 11 were reached:

```
reached:  make-dtree test-dtree predict-dtree make-forest test-forest predict-forest
          entropy make-refine-dataset make-refine-learner train-refine-learner
          test-refine-learner  (+ the train-refine-learner-process macro)
```

Regression accounted for 12 of the 38 unreached symbols despite having its own README section and four examples, and `pruning!` is a README headline feature. Both were picked first because their implementations are healthy — unlike `src/feature-importance.lisp` and `src/reconstruction.lisp`, which need fixing before they can be tested at all.

Also unreached, and still are: `gini`, `cross-validation-forest-with-refine-learner`, `predict-refine-learner`, and every non-default value of `:gain-test` / `:balance` / `:remove-sample-indices?` / `:save-parent-node?`.

## What is here

```
cl-random-forest-test/regression   t/regression.lisp   5 tests
cl-random-forest-test/pruning      t/pruning.lisp      5 tests
```

13 → 23 tests on SBCL, 9 → 19 on CCL.

**These are property assertions, not pinned accuracy numbers.** The existing 13 tests assert a hardcoded accuracy within `±1.0`, and those numbers carry authority because they were inherited from the original prove suite. A new test has nothing to inherit, and a number produced by one run of the code under test proves nothing about it. So these assert what the features are *for*: the forest beats a single tree, the model explains most of the signal, refinement improves on the forest, pruning actually removes leaves, accuracy survives pruning. Every threshold has its measured range recorded in a comment beside it.

**They run offline.** The other 13 suites all download LIBSVM datasets; these use deterministic synthetic data generated in `t/fixture.lisp` and finish in about a second each. Each generator seeds its own LCG rather than sharing one, so a suite sees identical data whether it runs alone or inside the full run.

## Three tests deliberately assert the library is broken

Issues #14, #15 and #16 are open. Rather than skip those paths or leave CI red, three tests pin the current behaviour, each with a comment saying so:

| test | pins |
|---|---|
| `regression-refine-learner-default-gamma-diverges` | #16 — the default `gamma` of 0.99 overflows the sparse RLS covariance |
| `pruning-strands-leaves-without-sample-indices` | #14 — `delete-children!` never restores `node-sample-indices` |
| `pruning-does-not-update-forest-n-leaf` | #15 — `forest-n-leaf` goes stale after pruning |

When one of them starts **failing**, the bug underneath it has been fixed. Each comment says that explicitly so nobody "repairs" the test.

## What `pruning-rate` actually does

`pruning-reduces-leaf-count` asserts the real contract, which is not the one the README describes:

```
leaves deleted = floor(number of leaf-parents * pruning-rate)
```

`pruning!` prunes leaf-*parents*, and each pruned parent loses two children while becoming a leaf itself — a net loss of one. Exact at rates 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5. The README says rate 0.1 deletes 10% of leaves; it deletes about 3.7%. Filed as #18; not fixed here.

## A CI hole this uncovered, and closed

On CCL, a failing test did **not** fail CI. The aggregate's `(error "Tests failed.")` fired correctly, then CCL dropped into its interactive debugger, hit EOF on stdin, and exited 0 — the job went green with a red suite. `t/run-test.ros` now handles `serious-condition` and exits 1.

`serious-condition` rather than `error` on purpose: `storage-condition` (heap exhaustion — the suite builds 500-tree forests under `dynamic-space-size=2048`) and `sb-sys:interactive-interrupt` are not `error`s, and would have escaped into the same debugger.

## Two implementation differences worth knowing

Both surfaced as green-locally, red-on-CI, and neither is reproducible on the development machine.

**Float overflow traps.** x86-64 SBCL and CCL trap it and signal `floating-point-overflow`; aarch64 SBCL does not and quietly produces NaN, ignoring even an explicit `set-floating-point-modes :traps` request. The `#16` pin accepts either manifestation.

**Type declarations.** SBCL checks the `(simple-array fixnum)` declaration in `class-distribution` and signals `type-error` on a stranded leaf. CCL does not check it: `(length nil)` is 0, the leaf returns a zero distribution, and prediction returns a quietly wrong answer instead of a loud one. That is why the `#14` pin counts leaves whose `node-sample-indices` is `NIL` rather than catching a condition — the count is identical on both implementations, and drops to zero the moment `delete-children!` is fixed.

## Verification

CI green at `63aea6d` on sbcl/ubuntu (30 assertions), sbcl/macOS (29) and ccl/ubuntu (26), zero failures.

The failure path was verified too, on a throwaway branch carrying a deliberately failing test: all three jobs went red, and the CCL job ended with `Process completed with exit code 1` — no debugger prompt. A green run alone would not have shown that the safety net works.

Locally: 23 tests enumerated across the seven suites; both new suites confirmed to run without touching `dataset/` or spawning `wget`.

## Summary

This is the kickoff step for the vulnerability-class remediation harness: mechanically splitting OWASP Juice Shop into a **working copy** (`target-apps/juice-shop/`, what the harness will actually scan/fix/test against) and a **separate, private answer key** (`juice-shop-answer-key` repo, used once at final scoring, never touched during harness development) — so that any accuracy numbers the harness reports later are earned, not read off the answer key.

- `tools/blind-development/split_answer_key.py` — the extraction script. Reads a pristine `juice-shop/juice-shop` clone and produces both sides:
  - strips all `vuln-code-snippet` comment tags repo-wide (174 occurrences / 14 files — broader than the ~50/7 files visible from a narrower grep, since the tags also live in the Angular frontend, `server.ts`, `.sol` contracts, and `securityQuestions.yml`)

  - neutralizes all 95 `challengeUtils.solveIf(challenge, criteria)` scoring-oracle call sites in application source (37 files) — replacing only the criteria argument, and explicitly *not* touching `test/**`, since some unit tests legitimately call `solveIf` directly to test the mechanism itself
  - patches `routes/vulnCodeFixes.ts` to degrade gracefully instead of crashing now that `codefixes/` is gone
  - strips `hints`/`description`/`mitigationUrl` from `challenges.yml` (zeroed, not deleted — `datacreator.ts` does an unconditional `.replace()` on `description` at boot)
  - splits 219 exploit-payload test cases out of `test/api/*.test.ts`, `test/cypress/e2e/*.spec.ts`, and `test/server/*.unit.test.ts` into answer-key mirrors, keeping the functional/regression subset in the working copy
  - 12 additional hand-verified fixes for a second, non-generalized scoring-oracle pattern (`notSolved(...)/solve(...)` inline blocks) found in 5 files
- `docs/BLIND_DEVELOPMENT.md` — the protocol, what each phase does and why, verification results, and known limitations
- `target-apps/juice-shop/` — the resulting stripped working copy
- `README.md` — updated to describe the project and the guardrail: **no harness-development session may open, read, or reference the answer-key repo.**

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `npm run test:server`: 247/247 pass
- `npm run test:api`: 466/474 pass — the 8 failures are all in `test/api/internet-resources.test.ts`, which needs live network access to pastebin.com/stackoverflow.com unavailable in this sandbox (confirmed with a direct `curl`); not caused by the strip

items.title: feat(sparq-nlq): exec-accuracy harness — answer-F1, oracle vs end-to-end, grounded vs not (sq-05rv)
items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Implements bead **sq-05rv** — the design doc's `sparq-nlq` accuracy gate (`research/genai-design.md` §4, `sparq-nlq` row): an end-to-end **exec-accuracy** harness for NL→SPARQL that grades the *executed* query the QALD way and reports the two axes the doc demands **separately**.

## What it grades

- **Answer-set F1**, not query-string equality (`research/genai-nl-to-sparql.md` §1, §4.2). Both the candidate and a **gold** query are executed on the *same* graph and their bind-row sets compared — gold answers are recomputed live, so there is no checked-in answer blob to drift (§4.3).
- **Oracle-linking vs end-to-end**, reported separately: oracle feeds the correct query through the same validate→execute path (isolating the engine-side loop from the model's linking); end-to-end has the model write the query.
- **Grounded vs the same LLM ungrounded** — `Comparison::headline_grounding_pays()` is the load-bearing check that grounded end-to-end macro-F1 **>** ungrounded ("the grounding must pay for itself"). New `NlqConfig::ground` (default `true`) toggles the schema deck in the prompt; the two prompts are distinct strings, so no `ReplayLlm` collision.

## CI is fully offline — by construction

The gate does **not** depend on a live LLM or the network:

| Layer | What | Runs in CI? |
|---|---|---|
| `harness_demonstrates_grounding_pays_in_memory` | tiny in-memory graph + scripted backends (grounded model answers from the deck; ungrounded one hallucinates a predicate) — proves the harness + the headline inequality deterministically | **yes, always** |
| `olympics_exec_accuracy_replay` | answer-F1 on the real 1.78M-triple olympics dataset via the committed `ReplayLlm` fixture + oracle linking | yes, **skip-if-absent** dataset |
| `live_exec_accuracy` | the real-model measurement, records replay fixtures, asserts the inequality | **no** — `#[cfg(feature = "live")]` **and** `#[ignore]`'d |

## Honest status (no overclaim)

This validates the **harness** and the **mechanism** of the headline claim on scripted/recorded completions. It does **not** yet produce a real model's accuracy **numbers** — that requires the `live_exec_accuracy` run (`--features live` + `RecordingLlm`, network + key + dataset), which is `#[ignore]`'d out of the gate so a model/network outage never reds the build. After a live run the recorded fixtures become the offline regression set. README "Honest status" updated to say exactly this.

items.title: feat(corpus): disclose input composition — only 8.9% came from a rendered page
items.body:
BR-0. The corpus is used as a **document extraction** benchmark, but **91% of its documents never existed as a rendered page**. That was undisclosed, and it scopes every accuracy number in this repo.

## Measured across all 1,114 manifests

| Tier | Input | Docs | % |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| A1 | Image → OCR | 52 | 4.7% |
| A2 | PDF → parse | 47 | 4.2% |
| A3 | Office → parse | 3 | 0.3% |
| B | HTML → markdown | 399 | 35.8% |
| C | Plain text | 150 | 13.5% |
| D | Authored markdown | 463 | 41.6% |

**99 documents (8.9%) came from a rendered page.** And of the 648 documents labelled *real*, only **99 (15.3%)** did — the rest are clean EDGAR HTML or plain-text transcriptions.

## Why this matters for the headline finding

The corpus's central result compares *real* vs *synthetic*. But the real set is **itself mostly clean input**. So the measured real-vs-synthetic gap **understates** the true clean-vs-messy delta — a real set drawn from scans and layout-heavy PDFs would widen it, not narrow it. It should be reported as a **lower bound**.

## A suggestive pattern, not yet a result

`receipts` is the only category composed **entirely** of rendered-page input (52/52, image→OCR). It is also the **lowest-accuracy category in the corpus at 81.0%** — 9pp below the next lowest.

That is consistent with parse quality being a dominant term, but it is **not established here**: document length is an obvious confound (`contracts` is 90.8% on clean HTML, and the paper attributes that to 50+ page documents). Establishing it needs the controlled paired ablation — BR-0b Track A, render the same ground-truth documents to PDF and degrade them along a ladder. This PR is the disclosure; that experiment is the test.

## What's in the PR

- **`scripts/composition_report.py`** — derives the breakdown from manifests, so it can't drift from reality. `--check` mode for CI.
- **`docs/composition.md`** — the generated disclosure.
- **CI gate** — the build fails if the report goes stale, so the disclosure cannot silently rot as the corpus changes. Guard verified to actually fire.
- **`README.md`** — warning placed directly above the accuracy table, where the numbers are.

## Note on counts

This PR surfaces a provenance discrepancy worth reconciling separately: the script classifies **648 real / 466 synthetic**, the README says **669 / 431**, and the paper says **669 / 445**. The script classifies from `source_name`; the others are hand-maintained. Not fixed here — flagging it.

## Docs checklist

- [x] `docs/composition.md` added, generated and CI-gated
- [x] `README.md` updated in the same PR
- [ ] N/A — no schema or engine behaviour changed; no bench run required (no documents added, removed, or altered)

items.title: GA-readiness fixes: silent-zero-execution hole, timeout diagnostics, honest detector claims
items.body:
## Why

The 2026-08-03 GA evaluation found that the core engine is close to release quality but that several findings stood between the library and an honest GA: a silent-zero-execution hole, discarded diagnostics on the highest-value failure path, and detection claims the code does not support. This PR fixes everything from that evaluation except the two items that are the maintainer's call (the license-gate default and cutting 1.7.0).

## What

- **`invocations`/`threads` below 1 are rejected at `AsyncTestConfig.build()`.** `@AsyncTest(invocations = 0)` previously reported a passing test whose body never ran, because the interceptor had already called `invocation.skip()`. `threads = 0` failed only as `new CyclicBarrier(0)` deep inside the round.
- **Round timeouts keep the failures the completed workers produced**, as suppressed exceptions on the round-timeout error. Before, 5 real assertion errors plus 3 hung workers reported only a thread count.
- **One INFO line per JVM (`runner.agent.absent`) when agent-backed detection is inactive.** A bare `@AsyncTest` under the "127 detectors" banner detects almost nothing without the agent or explicit recording calls (pinned by `DetectionCoverageTest`); now the runtime says so instead of staying silent.
- **The detector-accuracy eval exists and its numbers are published** (`docs/analysis/detector-accuracy-eval.md`, enforced by `DetectorAccuracyEvalTest`): 6 of 6 buggy variants fire; 3 of 6 correctly synchronized twins stay silent. The three that fire on correct code share one cause: no representation of locks. Those false positives are pinned so improvement shows up as a red test.
- **Shared-instance detector reports say what they observe.** All 17 `Shared*` detectors now state the conditional fact (unsynchronized use corrupts X) and close with "the detector observes sharing, not locks". `SharedSecureRandomDetector` drops HIGH to MEDIUM with an explicit severity marker: `java.security.SecureRandom` documents instances as thread-safe and the JDK providers synchronize internally, so HIGH failed `failOn = HIGH` builds over the documented-safe idiom. Security review of the three security-listed crypto detectors is in the commit message of 6938eb5: detection fires on identical inputs, MessageDigest/StatefulCrypto keep HIGH and their corruption consequences.
- **`FalseSharingDetector` findings are gated behind `-Dasync-test.experimental.false-sharing=true`.** Its offsets are declaration-order arithmetic the JVM's real layout does not follow, keying is per class, and the pair predicate excludes the textbook all-threads case; findings uncorrelated with the phenomenon must be opt-in.
- **`docs/analysis/comparison.md` no longer claims ThreadSanitizer cannot detect races.** The table now states each tool's real capabilities, with jcstress added as the honest Java-side comparison.
- The README's detector bullet now discloses the zero-config vs instrumented split, and docs quoting the old report wording (catalog, skill table, two example READMEs) are updated in the same change.

## Verification

- Every behavior change was written failing-first and each commit message records the red run: the validation tests failed with "nothing was thrown", the timeout test failed with the worker's exception unreachable, the log-contract assertion saw 0 announcements, the SecureRandom severity assertions were red at HIGH, and the FalseSharing gate test was proven by forcing the property on globally and watching it go red.
- Full local `mvn clean verify` on JDK 21 with mock license: **BUILD SUCCESS in 14:55, 1709 + 43 + 5 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped**, including PMD, SpotBugs, Checkstyle, NullAway, JaCoCo thresholds and japicmp against 1.6.0. Not run locally: the JDK 25 leg (not installed) and PITest (on-demand only).

items.title: Add ACEC-Belief RAG design + implementation, reorganize repo layout
items.body:
## Summary

### 1. ACEC-Belief RAG (design + implementation)

Introduces **ACEC-Belief RAG** (Action-Conditioned Evidence-Coverage Belief), replacing the old pooled system-level Beta-Bernoulli `BeliefState` approach as the active research direction. Full design/theory: [ACEC_Belief_RAG_design.md](ACEC_Belief_RAG_design.md).

- Old belief system (`rag/src/belief/*.py`, not `acec/`) empirically gave ≤±0.3pt over the R3-RAG baseline — it tracked *component quality* (retrieval/LLM/noise), not *whether the question's required evidence has actually been found*. Kept in place, untouched, purely as an ablation baseline.
- ACEC instead tracks a **per-slot, per-question Bayesian coverage posterior**: for each dynamically-discovered evidence "slot" (a sub-goal like a bridge entity dependency), is it covered yet — action-indexed (EXPAND/REWRITE/DECOMPOSE route to different likelihoods) so the update is no longer confounded across unrelated retrieval actions.

New module `rag/src/belief/acec/`:
- `action_labeler.py` — routes free-form retrieval queries to (mode, target slot) via E5 cosine, no constrained decoding
- `coverage_belief.py` — the monotone per-slot coverage filter (p_j recursion, C_t / Var[C_t], VOI stopping diagnostic, bridge-targeting suggestion)
- `observation_model.py` — action/role/binding-indexed Beta densities + closed-form Bayesian hit-posterior update
- `k_posterior.py` — posterior over the number of required evidence slots K
- `reward.py` — potential-based R_cov shaping (policy-invariant per Ng, Harada & Russell 1999) + turn-level GRPO advantages

items.body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/generate_benchmark_report.py`, the measurement-integrity tool identified as the highest-leverage first step in a broader L2-vs-source-mode gap analysis: a single reproducible benchmark report (JSON + Markdown) plus a `--check` mode that diffs it against the committed table in `docs/reference/tool-comparison.md`, so future accuracy numbers stop silently drifting from the example catalog.

## Motivation

`docs/reference/tool-comparison.md`'s "Full-catalog benchmark" table was last generated against a 170-case catalog. `examples/` grew to 181 cases (PR #539, already reflected in `CHANGELOG.md`) without the benchmark doc being regenerated, and nothing caught the mismatch automatically. This is exactly the kind of drift a gap analysis of the project's L2/source-mode benchmarking flagged as the top-priority fix (P0): "Create one generated benchmark report ... All README and documentation counts should be generated from that artifact. CI should fail when catalog counts and published tables diverge."

Note on scope: this sandbox has no `castxml`, `abidiff`, or `abi-compliance-checker` installed, so I could not honestly regenerate the table's numeric Correct/Accuracy/FP/FN cells against the full 181-case catalog — doing so would mean fabricating numbers for a benchmark I didn't actually run. Instead this PR ships the tooling, fixes the stale heading count (170 → 181) with an explicit "pending regeneration" note on the table body, and adds a regression-tested check that will catch this class of drift going forward. A maintainer with the full toolchain can run `scripts/generate_benchmark_report.py --check` to regenerate the table body from a real run.

## Changes

- **`scripts/generate_benchmark_report.py`** (new) — wraps `benchmark_comparison.py` into one artifact: git commit, `ground_truth.json` sha256, tool versions, exact case list, per-lane accuracy/FP/FN/unsupported-error-timeout counts, wall time, and process-tree peak RSS (`resource.getrusage`), plus per-lane cache-state (live vs. frozen-competitor provenance — surfaces when a reported number is a live run vs. a cached result from a different abicheck commit). `--check` parses the doc's table and reports drift; the heading case-count is always checked (cheap, no external tools needed), per-lane numeric rows only on a full-catalog run.
- **`scripts/benchmark_comparison.py`** — factored `run_suite(args)` out of `main()` (pure refactor, verified with a smoke run before/after) so this and future tooling can drive a benchmark run programmatically instead of shelling out; `parse_args()` now accepts an `argv` override for the same reason.
- **`scripts/check_ai_readiness.py`** — new `doc-count-sync` anchor pinning the benchmark heading's case count to `examples/ground_truth.json` (this anchor is what actually caught the 170-vs-181 drift while writing this PR).
- **`docs/reference/tool-comparison.md`** — heading corrected to 181 cases; added a note that the table body is pending regeneration, without inventing new numbers.
- **`tests/test_generate_benchmark_report.py`** (new) — unit tests for the doc-table parser and drift-diff logic against the *real* committed doc (a regression guard for the exact bug above), plus synthetic-data tests for the Markdown renderer and cache-state helper. No compiler/castxml required.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — entry under `[Unreleased] / Added`.

items.title: feat: read the numbers in a text, and 两 wherever it multiplies
items.body:
**Stacked on #25** — review that one first; this is the second half of Phase 5,
and the diff will shrink to just this once #25 merges.

Two things, both from review feedback on #25.

## 两 or 二

You were right that 12,000 wants 一万两千, and my "only at the front" rule was
wrong. Looking it up properly made it more interesting: 现代汉语词典 has 二
before 百 and either before 千/万/亿 — and then says the 二 of 三万二千 and
两亿二千万 *cannot* be 两. So the prescription and what people say disagree, and
this is a choice rather than a rule:

```ts
numeralHanzi(12_000); // "一万两千" — the default
numeralHanzi(12_000, { liang: "leading" }); // "一万二千" — the 词典's own rule
numeralHanzi(12_000, { liang: "never" }); // "一万二千", and 二千 for 2,000 too
```

Nothing touches a 2 that is not a multiplier: 12 是十二, 200 是二百, 120,000 是
十二万.

## Numbers in text

`convert` now reads the digits it meets:

```ts
convert(dictionary, "我有3个苹果。"); // "Wǒ yǒu sān gè píngguǒ."
convert(dictionary, "1988年之后"); // "yī jiǔ bā bā nián zhīhòu"
convert(dictionary, "95%的人"); // "bǎifēnzhījiǔshíwǔ de rén"
convert(dictionary, "3D打印"); // "sān D dǎyìn"
```

Three rules pick the style, and they are deliberately few:

| The text | What happens | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| four digits before 年 | spelled out | 1997年 is a year; 30年 is thirty years |
| digits before % or ％ | 百分之, reversed | the sign is read, and read first |
| anything else | counted | what nearly every digit in running text is |

Measured first: of 7,846 digit runs over 88,866 lines of Tatoeba and
zh.wikipedia, the commonest things after them are 年 (2,107), 月 (1,366), 日
(1,044), then 人, 号, 点, 个, 岁 — so counting is the right default by a long
way, and years are the one case that needs saying.

**A read number is a word.** 25个 is `èrshíwǔ gè`, which is 正词法 6.1.5, so it
goes through `markWord` and takes the 隔音符号 like any other word — 20%。 is
`Bǎifēnzhī'èrshí.` Digits spelled out are *not* a word, so 1997年 is
`yī jiǔ jiǔ qī nián`. Sandhi crosses into the next run, which is what makes 1个
`yí gè`.

**A digit touching `:`, `-` or `/` is left exactly as written.** 6:30 is a time,
3202-5625 is a phone number, COVID-19 is a name. Found by measuring: the first
version read 6:30 as `liù:sānshí`, which is worse than not reading it.

**What it deliberately does not guess.** A bare four-digit year with nothing
after it — `他生于1990。` — is counted. 68% of four-digit runs sit directly
before 年 and are handled; of the rest, some are years in citations and some are
2000人 or 1500. Reading a quantity as a year is a *reading* error rather than a
spacing one, so the rule stops where the evidence does.

## What the end-to-end harness says

`pnpm numerals` now also converts CC-CEDICT's numeric headwords whole: **7 of 17
match**, and the ten that do not are all one thing — a bare number CC-CEDICT
reads as a label (110, 88, 996, 95后) where `convert` counts it. Nothing in
running text separates 我有110个 from 打110, so that is a limit with a number on
it rather than a defect.

## Checks

- `pnpm check` green: 975 tests, 100% statements/lines/functions.
- **Equivalence**: with `numbers: "keep"`, all **355,464** conversions over the
  corpora — four option sets including the greedy baseline and `convertPieces` —
  are byte-identical to before. The pipeline was restructured to decode runs
  before writing them (a number needs to see the next run), and this is what
  says nothing else moved.
- `pnpm accuracy`: five `numbers` cases added, all passing. Lattice exact 96.8%,
  readings 99.6%. The three misses are unchanged.
- The gold corpus guard now allows a lone Latin letter, since `sān D dǎyìn` is a
  legitimate expected output; everything else it checked, it still checks.
- README, `docs/numerals/`, `docs/options/`, `docs/converting/`,
  `docs/getting-started/`, `docs/html/` and `docs/cli/` updated together with
  their guards — four pages were showing `3Dyínháng`, which is no longer true.

items.title: feat: add recognition.mainThreadYieldMs for responsive main-thread web OCR
items.body:
## What

Adds `recognition.mainThreadYieldMs` (default `0`; the `/web` entry defaults it to `10` on the browser main thread), a pause before each recognition inference that yields the event loop so a page running `recognize()` without a Web Worker keeps painting and handling input instead of freezing for the whole image. Also exposed as `--main-thread-yield-ms` on the CLI.

## Why

On the main thread, WASM inference blocks the thread it runs on, and consecutive `await`s between inferences resolve as microtasks, which the renderer cannot interleave with. A script-tag setup with no worker therefore freezes the tab until the whole image is done.

This is a real adoption blocker: at least one downstream project ([cty-paddle-ocr](https://github.com/CraftThingy-Digital-Innovation/cty-paddle-ocr), a fork of the v3-era code) exists specifically to patch this, forcing sequential per-box processing with a `setTimeout` pause before each box. The rest of that fork's shims are already obsolete against the current `/web` entry; this option closes the one remaining gap so main-thread users can depend on the library directly.

## How

- `src/core/base-recognition.service.ts`: the pause lives in `runInference`, the single choke point all three strategies (`per-box`, `per-line`, `cross-line`) already funnel through. Strategies were already sequential, so the macrotask boundary was the only missing piece. `0` disables it and skips the timer entirely.
- `src/web/recognition.service.web.ts`: `withMainThreadYieldDefault` (exported for tests) injects the `10` default only when `typeof window !== "undefined" && !isWebWorker()`. Workers, Node, Bun, and React Native keep `0`. An explicit caller value, including an explicit `0`, always wins.
- `src/cli/options.ts` / `help.ts`: `--max-crop-source-side-length` sibling flag `--main-thread-yield-ms`, keeping the documented 1:1 option-to-flag mapping.
- Docs: README gets a "Main-Thread Usage (No Worker)" section (worker still recommended; detection's single inference still blocks briefly, only the recognition loop yields), plus rows in the `RecognitionOptions` and CLI flag tables; skill `SKILL.md` and `references/configuration.md` updated; CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]`.

### Benchmark (`bun bench/index.bench.ts`, receipt.jpg, default `mainThreadYieldMs: 0` so this exercises the disabled path)

Two samples on this branch (honest note: both are the branch; the worktree could not also check out `main`, so the baseline is main's published README numbers, 134-140 ms opencv at the same defaults on the same machine class):

```
Sample 1:
[per-box][opencv][noCache]             122.7 ms
[per-line][opencv][noCache]            114.4 ms
[cross-line][opencv][noCache]          115.7 ms
[per-box][canvas-native][noCache]      133.7 ms
[per-line][canvas-native][noCache]     128.3 ms
[cross-line][canvas-native][noCache]   134.2 ms

Sample 2:
[per-box][opencv][noCache]             133.6 ms
[per-line][opencv][noCache]            132.6 ms
[cross-line][opencv][noCache]          138.3 ms
[per-box][canvas-native][noCache]      148.0 ms
[per-line][canvas-native][noCache]     141.8 ms
[cross-line][canvas-native][noCache]   150.0 ms
```

The spread between the two samples (~10-15%) dwarfs anything the disabled path could add: with the default `0`, the change is one numeric comparison per inference, no timer is ever scheduled. Accuracy is byte-identical to main's published numbers on all six strategy/engine combinations (99.48/99.48/94.26 opencv, 99.48/99.22/94.78 canvas-native), in both samples. The enabled path costs ~10 ms per recognized line on main-thread web runs only, which is the point.

### Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally (`bun test`) - 260 pass, 0 fail (+4: a timer-spy test proving one yield fires per recognized line with accuracy intact, the CLI flag mapping case, and two unit tests for the main-thread/worker default branch)
- [x] Types are clean (`bun run type-check`)

### Compatibility

- [ ] Node.js (via `onnxruntime-node`)
- [x] Bun (via `onnxruntime-node`)
- [ ] Browser - WebAssembly fallback (Safari, older Firefox)
- [ ] Browser - WebGPU path (Chrome / Edge with a discrete or integrated GPU)

The browser rows are unticked because the main-thread default is covered by unit tests on the extracted branch logic, not by a manual browser session; a quick check on the live demo page after merge would be a good sanity pass.

items.title: Phase 1 (B031): Add quality-gate framework (TR golden set + eval tool + thresholds)
items.body:
## Scope

Adds the quality-gate framework needed to eventually mark B031 (real Ollama
NLU integration) as completed. This PR does **not** claim Ollama quality —
it builds the measurement infrastructure and reports an honest current
state: `NOT_EVALUATED` for live Ollama, because Ollama is not installed in
this environment.

## What's included

- `tests/fixtures/nlu_golden_tr.jsonl` — 50-example Turkish golden set
  (balanced: clear commands, ambiguous phrasing, typos/colloquial variants,
  out-of-whitelist intents, irreversible/approval-triggering actions).
- `tools/eval_nlu.py` — compares `mock` vs `ollama` on the same golden set;
  computes intent accuracy, entity match rate, parse-error rate, fallback
  rate, p50/p95 latency; writes `reports/nlu_eval_<YYYYMMDD>.md`. Never
  fabricates a result — if Ollama is unreachable it marks that column `N/A`
  with the reason, and returns `NOT_EVALUATED` rather than a false PASS.
- `tests/test_eval_nlu.py` — 30 tests covering loader/parser validation,
  metric computation, and fallback-vs-parse-error classification.
- `pyproject.toml` — `tools/` added to pytest `pythonpath`.
- `docs/BACKLOG.md` — B031 status updated to reflect the gate's existence
  and the still-open live-measurement gap.
- `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — new "Quality Gate" section (how to run, thresholds,
  troubleshooting) + a step-by-step "Canlı Ollama Kapanış Prosedürü"
  (start service → pull model → run eval → interpret → decide) for whoever
  closes B031 on a machine that actually has Ollama.
- `README.md` — short status note pointing at the gate.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` — ADR-014: golden-set + numeric-threshold methodology
  for "completed" claims on any NLU/AI component, not just this one.

## Test evidence

python -m pytest
============================= 132 passed in ~4.3s =============================

No regressions — all 102 pre-existing tests plus 30 new ones are green.

## Honest limitation

This development environment has **no Ollama** (`ollama` CLI not found,
`http://localhost:11434` refuses connection). The eval tool ran against
`mock` for real numbers (92.0% intent accuracy, reference only — mock never
produces entities, so its entity_match_rate is trivially 0%) and against
`ollama` which it correctly reports as `NOT_EVALUATED`, not a fabricated
pass or fail.

Mock provider entity extraction üretmez; entity metriği yalnızca Ollama canlı değerlendirmesinde gate kriteridir.

## Why B031 stays "partially completed"

The acceptance gate (5 thresholds: intent accuracy ≥90%, entity match
≥85%, parse-error ≤2%, fallback ≤5%, p95 latency ≤2.5s) is defined
specifically for the **live Ollama** path. Since that path has never
actually run against a real model, there is no evidence to support
"completed" — only that the measurement tooling itself is correct and
tested.

## Next step to close B031

On a host with Ollama installed:
ollama serve
ollama pull llama3
python tools/eval_nlu.py

If all 5 `ollama` thresholds show `PASS` in the generated report, update
`docs/BACKLOG.md` B031 to "Completed" referencing that report file. If any
threshold fails, keep it partial and record which metric(s) fell short —
see `docs/RUNBOOK.md` → "Canlı Ollama Kapanış Prosedürü" for the exact
decision procedure.

## Out of scope / unaffected

- Financial execution (T18–T20) — untouched, still paused (ADR-011).
- Risk/approval flow (T13) — untouched; `RUN_DELETE_FILE` still triggers
  `WAITING_APPROVAL` regardless of NLU provider.
- `translate_and_extract()` contract — unchanged (established in the prior
  B031 PR, not touched here).

items.title: Make the accuracy claim reproducible: report metadata + mechanical scoring
items.body:
Implements **ТЗ №5** — make the accuracy claim reproducible. The claim couldn't be reproduced or diffed because no report recorded how it was produced. Fixed end to end.

## 1. Run metadata in the report ⚠️ breaking `--json-out` format

`--json-out` was a bare findings list. It's now an object:

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "tool": "mem-audit",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "run_at": "2026-07-26T12:00:00+00:00",
    "user_id": "demo",
    "embedder": { "provider": "github", "model": "openai/text-embedding-3-small", "base_url": "https://models.github.ai/inference" },
    "judge": { "provider": "cerebras", "model": "gpt-oss-120b", "base_url": "https://api.cerebras.ai/v1" },
    "params": { "top_k": 5, "min_similarity": 0.3, "similarity_threshold": null, "max_retries": 5, "min_request_interval": 12.0, "page_size": 500 },
    "memories_scanned": 9,
    "candidate_pairs": 4,
    "judge_verdicts": { "DUPLICATE": 1, "CONTRADICTION": 1, "UPDATE": 1, "UNRELATED": 1, "skipped": 0 }
  },
  "findings": [
    { "type": "contradiction", "severity": "high", "memory_ids": ["m1", "m2"], "summary": "Contradiction: \"My name is LGY\" vs \"My name is LGS\"", "detail": "…", "suggested_action": "…" },
    { "type": "stale", "severity": "medium", "memory_ids": ["m3", "m4"], "summary": "Likely superseded: \"I live in Berlin\" -> \"I live in Madrid\"", "detail": "…", "suggested_action": "…" },
    { "type": "duplicate", "severity": "low", "memory_ids": ["m5", "m6"], "summary": "Duplicate: \"I enjoy playing chess…\" ~ \"I like playing chess…\"", "detail": "…", "suggested_action": "…" }
  ]
}
```

(Above is the actual offline-demo report, `detail`/`suggested_action` elided for width.)

- `version` comes from `importlib.metadata` (not hardcoded); it reads `0+unknown` on a bare source checkout, the real version once pip-installed.
- **`model` is the actual model used** (preset default or `--*-model` override); `base_url` records where it went. **No API keys anywhere** (asserted in tests).
- **Judge verdict distribution** over all four labels + `skipped` (rate-limit-exhausted pairs).
- Threaded via an optional `report_metadata` dict through `run_audit → find_contradictions`. Defaults `None`, so library callers/tests are unaffected and the bare-list partial format is preserved for them.
- **Incremental atomic write preserved**: with metadata, the partial file is the same `{metadata, findings}` object and stays valid JSON on interruption (test added, `KeyboardInterrupt` mid-run → object with the completed findings + live verdict tally).
- Console gains one dim line under the table: `embedder: … · judge: … · top-k: N`.

## 2. `analyze_confidence_test.py` scores itself

Was a checklist asking a human to match paraphrased summaries. Now mechanical:

- `confidence_test_seed.py` captures each Mem0 id at seed time and writes `confidence_ground_truth.json` (pair name → the two ids + expected type) next to the config.
- `analyze_confidence_test.py` matches findings to pairs **by memory id**, prints recall, precision, correct-type vs right-pair-wrong-type, false positives, misses, and the run metadata. `score(findings, pairs)` is a pure stdlib function.
- **`tests/test_confidence_analysis.py`** reconstructs the documented run as data and asserts `score` → **recall 7/7, precision 7/10**, correct-type 5, wrong-type 2, 3 FPs — so the headline number is reproducible in CI with no keys. (I could not run the live seed/analyze against a real store — no keys — so the end-to-end "on the current `confidence_report.json`" check is proven via this reconstruction, not a live run.)

## 3. README "Measured accuracy" rewritten

All three runs, numbers side by side (recall 7/7 every time; runs 2 & 3 byte-identical — same 76 candidate pairs, same 10 findings — so **not** LLM sampling noise; run 1 = 7 findings / 0 FPs vs 10 / 3 FPs later, with 2 update pairs typed CONTRADICTION). States plainly that the cause is not established and not recoverable (old reports stored no versions/params), lists what was ruled out, and gives the reader guidance: rely on recall, verify type and absence of extras by eye. No "generally stable"; no claim of LLM non-determinism.

## Commands run (clean venv: numpy rich click only — CI condition)

- `py_compile` over `mem_audit examples tests` → OK
- all **9** test files → pass (incl. `test_confidence_analysis`, `test_report` object form, `test_resilience` verdict/interrupt, `test_pipeline` metadata)
- `python examples/demo_offline.py` → OK
- `python examples/demo_offline.py --json-out r.json` → writes the `{metadata, findings}` object above; verified all 9 metadata keys present, `judge_verdicts` populated, **no `api_key` substring**
- `dev-scripts/analyze_confidence_test.py --report … --ground-truth …` on a synthetic report → prints recall/precision/metadata correctly
- README tariff grep → empty

## Not verified (no live keys)
A full audit against a real Mem0 store, and the live seed→run→analyze loop. The metadata plumbing and scorer are proven offline; I did not fabricate a live green run.

## Acceptance
- Clean-venv tests green (9 files); CI matrix 3.10/3.11/3.12.
- Offline demo works; `--json-out` in the demo yields a metadata file.
- Interrupted run leaves valid JSON (test).
- No API keys in the report (test).
- Accuracy section has all three runs' numbers.
- Full new report format shown above.

items.title: feat: machine-readable OAuth compatibility list
items.body:
Vendors publish their Basic auth advisories one at a time, as prose, PDFs and
support pages. There is no single place to check whether the thing on your
network has a way out. This is an attempt at one.

`data/devices.json` holds fourteen entries; `docs/DEVICE-COMPATIBILITY.md`
renders them.

## Why structured rather than another table

A JSON file can be read by a script. The audit script could eventually flag
"the mailbox is exposed *and* the device behind it is on the ruled-out list",
which is a decision rather than a report.

The wider reason is links. This project cannot ask anyone for backlinks
without it reading as spam, and it will not rank for the generic queries
before December. What it can do is be the list somebody cites when answering
a forum question about an ineo 266 — because no such list exists.

## Enforced rather than encouraged

**Every entry needs an evidence URL.** The build refuses one without it: a
compatibility list is only worth citing if each row can be checked, and that
property survives only if it cannot be skipped.

The table is generated, and CI runs `--check`. That job is deliberately *not*
gated on the `changes` job — hand-editing the generated page touches no code
file, so a gate on `code == 'true'` would skip precisely the case worth
catching. Verified all three failure modes locally: drift, missing evidence,
unknown status value.

## On accuracy

Only what the advisories document is encoded. No model numbers from memory.

Where a vendor publishes a long, revised per-model list (Ricoh), the entry
says `check-advisory` rather than reproducing numbers that would go stale and
be wrong in someone's hands. Where no public per-model statement was found
(Kyocera), the entry says that rather than implying one exists.

Konica Minolta's is the entry that matters: those ineo models are marked
"N/A" in the vendor's own OAuth column, and the advisory points their owners
at a different mail service instead of an update.

## Also

`docs/ERROR-MESSAGES.md` and `docs/NO-OAUTH-FIRMWARE.md` from the previous two
PRs are cross-linked, and both READMEs and the docs index point at the list.

items.title: Release v1.3.1
items.body:
## Release Information

- **Release Version:** v1.3.1
- **Release Date:** 2026-08-09
- **Release Type:** Patch
- **Release Branch:** `release/1.3.x`
- **Target Branch:** `main`

## Release Summary

Adds `SiteContext::isPinned()`. Purely additive — one new accessor, no behaviour change to anything that already existed.

`currentSiteId()` answers `null` in two situations that are not the same thing: nothing is pinned and the resolver found nothing, or calling code pinned "no site" on purpose through `setSiteId( null )` or `withoutSite()`. Most consumers can treat both alike and leave their queries unscoped. A package that falls back to a default site of its own cannot — `null` meaning "nothing in context" is its cue to apply that default, while `null` meaning "no site, deliberately" is an instruction from another package to stay unscoped. Without a way to separate them it substitutes its default and scopes work that was meant to span every site.

The `$pinned` flag already tracked the distinction internally. This release only makes it readable.

Surfaced by the `artisanpack-ui/analytics` v1.5.0 release review (finding M7), where `TenantManager` was overriding a sibling package's explicit no-site pin with analytics' `default_site_id`. Analytics 1.5.0 requires `^1.3.1` for this and cannot have its lock refreshed until this ships.

## Changelog

### Added

- **`SiteContext::isPinned()`** — reports whether a site was put in context explicitly through `setSiteId()`, `forSite()`, or `withoutSite()`. Reachable through the `ArtisanPackSite` facade.

- Nothing.

**Issues Fixed:**

- None — surfaced by the `artisanpack-ui/analytics` v1.5.0 release review rather than a reported issue.

**Related PRs:**

A new method on a concrete class that nothing outside this package implements. Applications on 1.3.0 upgrade with no changes.

items.title: Update model builder for gpt-oss
items.body:
# Update model builder for GPT-OSS (QMoE encoding fix, decoupled INT4/INT8 quantization, QK-norm fusion)

## Description

This PR overhauls the Python model builder to correctly export GPT-OSS (and related MoE/hybrid) models. It fixes a CUDA QMoE expert-weight encoding bug that produced garbage INT4 weights, decouples the INT4 quantization *method* from INT8 bit *placement* (so any base method can be combined with any INT8 upgrade policy), adds per-channel QMoE quantization, and introduces optional Q/K-norm fusion into `GroupQueryAttention`. It supersedes #2209.

## Summary of Changes

### QMoE expert-weight quantization (CUDA)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New `_cutlass_prepacked_blockwise_quantize` quantizes each expert `[N, K]` with ONNX Runtime's blockwise `quantize_matmul_4bits`/`8bits` on the transposed `[K, N]` weight, **keeps the signed scales**, and offline CUTLASS-prepacks via `pack_weights_for_cuda_mixed_gemm(..., force_arch=80)` — the exact encoding validated by the `com.microsoft` QMoE CUDA parity tests. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New `_matmulnbits_blockwise_quantize` emits raw `[N, K/pack]` weights + blockwise scales for the runtime PrePack hook (used when `qmoe_weights_prepacked=0`). |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New `_symmetric_per_channel_quantize` / `_cuda_per_channel_quantize` add per-channel QMoE quantization (`qmoe_block_size <= 0`), omitting the `block_size` attribute. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | `make_qmoe_weights` routes CUDA QMoE through the prepacked/raw/per-channel paths, validates `block_size ∈ {32, 64, 128}` and `N % pack == 0` with real exceptions, and removes the deprecated column-wise (TensorRT-LLM) path. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New tri-state `weights_prepacked` QMoE attribute (`-1` auto/omit, `1` prepacked, `0` raw), CUDA-only, validated to `{-1, 0, 1}`; override via `extra_options["qmoe_weights_prepacked"]`. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/gptoss.py](src/python/py/models/builders/gptoss.py) | Always transpose HF expert weights to output-major `[E, N, K]` for **all** EPs (the old CUDA-only special case swapped `N`/`K` and silently corrupted quantized weights/scales). |

**Root cause fixed:** the previous CUDA path applied `abs()` to the blockwise scales. `quantize_matmul_4bits` folds the block-anchor sign into the scale and the kernel dequantizes as `(q − 8) · scale`, so `abs()` corrupted every block whose anchor element is negative (~half the blocks), yielding garbage weights that merely *looked* like INT4 quality loss.

### Decoupled INT4 method vs. INT8 bit placement

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [src/python/py/models/builder.py](src/python/py/models/builder.py) | New orthogonal flags `last_matmul_weight_int8`, `int8_mixed_layers`, `int8_linear_attn`; `int4_algo_config` reduced to base methods `default`/`rtn`/`k_quant` with help text updated. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New `resolve_int4_quant_config` splits `int4_algo_config` into a base method + placement flags; legacy compound names (`rtn_last`, `k_quant_last`, `k_quant_mixed`, `k_quant_linear`) are kept as aliases. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New `make_bit_placement_config` builds the per-node INT8 `customized_weight_config`; `make_algo_config` now takes a base method + config and raises on unknown methods. |
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | `to_int4` supports INT8 placement on top of the DEFAULT method via a two-pass scheme (INT4 body first, then an **RTN** INT8 pass for designated nodes, since DEFAULT 8-bit QOperator output is not consumed correctly by the runtime kernel). |
| [src/python/py/models/quantization.md](src/python/py/models/quantization.md) | New doc explaining base methods, INT8 placement flags, legacy aliases, accuracy notes (MMLU numbers), and examples. |

### Q/K-norm fusion into GroupQueryAttention

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py) | New `is_fused_qk_norm_gqa_supported` and `q_norm_weight`/`k_norm_weight` GQA inputs to pass Q/K-norm weights directly into `GroupQueryAttention` (CUDA/WebGPU). Gated by the `fuse_qk_norm_gqa` extra option (default off). |
| [src/python/py/models/builder.py](src/python/py/models/builder.py) | Register `fuse_qk_norm_gqa` extra option. |
| [src/python/py/models/README.md](src/python/py/models/README.md) | Document the QK-norm fusion toggle. |

### Robustness / misc

- [src/python/py/models/builders/base.py](src/python/py/models/builders/base.py): `enable_skip_layer_norm_strict_mode` is now version-gated — disabled on ONNX Runtime ≥ 1.27 (FP32 accumulation by default, faster) and kept enabled on older supported versions to avoid an accuracy regression (new `onnxruntime_version_at_least` helper).
- Error chaining (`raise ... from e`) added to QMoE quantization failures.

### Tests

- [test/python/builder/test_qmoe_weights.py](test/python/builder/test_qmoe_weights.py): New unit tests covering CUDA path dispatch (prepacked/raw/per-channel), EP gating, unsupported block-size rejection, per-channel shapes, and a regression guard asserting blockwise scales stay **signed**. Includes a hardened dependency stub that no longer shadows a real `onnxruntime` wheel.

## Testing

- Run the new builder unit tests:
  ```bash
  python -m pytest -sv test/python/builder/test_qmoe_weights.py
  ```
  CUDA-only shape/sign regression tests auto-skip when the ONNX Runtime CUDA pybind (`quantize_matmul_4bits`, `pack_weights_for_cuda_mixed_gemm`) is unavailable.
- End-to-end: build a GPT-OSS QMoE model on CUDA and verify generation quality (the encoding fix restores expected INT4 accuracy vs. the previous garbage output).
- Backward compatibility: legacy `int4_algo_config` compound values (`rtn_last`, `k_quant_last`, `k_quant_mixed`, `k_quant_linear`) still produce identical models via the alias mapping.

## Motivation and Context

Replaces #2209. The CUDA QMoE export path was producing weights the `com.microsoft` QMoE kernel could not consume correctly (sign-stripped scales + wrong `N`/`K` orientation), which manifested as severe quality loss on GPT-OSS / Qwen3.5 MoE models. Alongside the fix, the quantization configuration surface is reworked so INT4 rounding method and INT8 placement are independent, which is needed for the mixed-precision recipes these models rely on.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Documentation updated (`quantization.md`, `README.md`)
- [x] No breaking changes (legacy `int4_algo_config` values preserved as aliases)
- [ ] CI passes

items.title: v4 scaffold: theory-guided dastgah classifier
items.body:
## What changed

- **Dastgah_Classifier_v4** scaffold, starting from the v3 phrase-aware melodic pipeline. The [v4 README](Dastgah_Classifier_v4/README.md) lays out the design goals: ist/forud-guided tonic detection, shahed features (emphasis-weighted pitch-class profile + tonic→shahed interval), Farhat-derived interval templates, cents-level resolution around the neutral (koron) intervals, and segment voting with abstention for modulating gushehs.
- **v4 measurement rules**: group-aware splits (same-album tracks never span train/eval) and 5-fold grouped CV for all headline numbers — single 86-track test splits swing ±7 accuracy points between seeds on the current 570-track dataset.
- **analysis/tonic_audit.py**: diagnostic comparing three independent tonic candidates (per-segment vote, pooled argmax, phrase-final/forud-weighted) on correct vs misclassified test tracks from both rebaseline seeds. Its outcome gates which theory feature lands first.
- **v3**: `tonic_strategy` default flipped to `vote` (the CV-validated production setting); tests updated; README documents conservative laptop worker defaults.
- **v2**: `models/model_config.json` `cache_dir` made relative so the checked-in config is portable.

## Why

The dataset expansion to 570 tracks reset all baselines: the production v3 config now scores test acc 0.59–0.66 across seeds (was 0.765 on the old 340-track split). The persistent confusions (Segah↔Shur, weak Homayun) are exactly the ones scale-content models make on modes that differ by note *function* (shahed/ist/forud) rather than note *inventory* — v4 exists to encode that theory instead of hoping the model rediscovers it from ~100 tracks per class.

## Notes for review

- v4 currently trains identically to v3 (same CLI, shared feature cache); the theory features land in follow-up PRs gated on the tonic audit.
- Baseline run artifacts (metrics, splits) live in gitignored `runs/`/`data/` dirs; numbers are recorded in the v4 README.

items.body:
## Summary

Evaluates mnemonist's RAG/memory pipeline end-to-end, fixes the issues that surfaced, and brings the docs and benchmarks in line with what the code actually does.

The architecture holds up well — **retrieval recall is 96.4%**, latency is sub-millisecond to 10k docs, Hebbian reinforcement measurably improves recall over time, and TurboQuant is near-lossless. The softer end-to-end accuracy numbers are bounded by off-the-shelf model choices (a general 384-dim embedder, a small reader), not by the design.

## Measured results (Apple M4 Pro; full detail + provenance in `docs/benchmarks.md`)

**Code retrieval — RAG over real repos** (new benchmark; none existed before). 78 intent-based gold queries across fsrc/sr/teasr/saige/mnemonist, run in an isolated `$HOME` so the real `~/.mnemonist` is untouched:

| | recall@1 | recall@5 | recall@10 | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overall (macro) | 34% | **72%** | **81%** | 0.50 |

**LongMemEval — conversational memory:**
- Retrieval recall@5 **96.4%**
- End-to-end QA **37.2%** (500 q; reader gpt-4o-mini, judge gpt-4o, top-5) — single-session-assistant 87.5%, hard reasoning types lower (reader-limited, not retrieval-limited)
- Latency p99 **406µs at 10k docs**
- Temporal reinforcement **+9.4pp** recall over 10 cycles
- TurboQuant **effectively lossless** at 8–10× compression

## Fixes

- **`fix(core)`** — HNSW `remove()` picked an arbitrary node as the new entry point, breaking the top-layer invariant and degrading recall after `forget`/decay. Now picks the highest-level node (+ regression test).
- **`feat(cli)`** — `--attend` glob was a no-op (never scoped ingestion); now implemented. `--format` was declared but inert; now wired (`json` compact default / `human` pretty).
- **`feat(evals)`** — QA fed user-turns-only context (assistant-sourced answers were impossible); now emits full transcripts + dates. Storage experiment had no raw baseline to measure quantization degradation against; added one.
- **`fix(ci)`** — `just eval` recipe referenced a nonexistent `mnemonist-evals` crate.

## Docs

Corrected drift verified against code: removed tree-sitter claims (the code uses `ChunkingStrategy`/`ParagraphChunking`), fixed the 4-crate → 2-crate structure, made TurboQuant and the training pipeline honestly labeled as research modules (not wired into `learn`/`remember`), removed the phantom `ctx` command, documented `update`/`version` and hidden config keys, and filled every `TBD` benchmark cell. Benchmark results mirror into the README via the existing `fsrc` directive.

## New tooling

- `scripts/rag_eval.py` — reproducible code-retrieval benchmark (`uv run`), gold sets in `docs/benchmarks/rag_gold/`.
- `scripts/longmemeval_qa.py` — the missing Phase B/C for Experiment 6 (LLM answer generation + LLM-judge scoring, with retry/backoff).

## Testing

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` (clean), and `cargo test --workspace` (151 core + 19 integration + 2 validation, all passing). Benchmarks reproducible via `just bench` / `just longmemeval` / the scripts above.

items.title: Add aggressive sharpening edits and improve evaluation metrics
items.body:
## Summary

This PR extends the robustness evaluation with two new sharpening edits and significantly improves the evaluation metrics and visualization to handle larger test sets (up to 100 images).

## Key Changes

### New Sharpening Edits
- **Unsharp mask sharpening** (`sharpen_usm_300pct`): An aggressive fixed convolution at 300% strength with 3px radius, serving as a baseline sharpening attack
- **AI super-resolution sharpening** (`sharpen_ai_x4`): A Real-ESRGAN x4 model that re-renders images and resamples back to original size, representing a generative attack that rewrites high-frequency detail rather than amplifying it
- New `ai_sharpen.py` module handles lazy loading of the ~4.7 MB model, device selection (CUDA/MPS/CPU), and tiled inference to bound memory usage

### Enhanced Evaluation Metrics
- Added **10th percentile bit accuracy** (`p10_raw_bit_accuracy`) to better characterize tail behavior in larger runs
- Added **payload loss count** (`n_payloads_lost`) to the summary
- Added **worst images list** showing the 5 hardest images per condition
- Improved console output with per-image failure reporting and progress tracking with ETA

### Adaptive Visualization
- Charts now adapt to dataset size: under 25 images shows individual dots with numbers; over 25 images switches to:
  - Violin plots showing distributions instead of individual points
  - Heatmap sorted worst-first (by mean accuracy) for pattern recognition
  - Markers instead of numbers in heatmap cells (○ for detected-but-lost, ✕ for undetected)
- Diverging red-grey-blue colormap centered on error-correction limit, making the pass/fail boundary visually obvious
- Added per-image ranking table showing which images struggle most across edits

### Infrastructure Improvements
- Added `--edits` and `--keep` flags to `02_edit.py` for selective re-running (important for the slow AI edit)
- Edit preflight checks allow graceful degradation when dependencies unavailable (e.g., no network for model download)
- Better progress reporting with timing estimates for long runs
- Removed `textwrap` dependency from evaluation script

### Documentation
- Updated README with new edits table and explanation of sharpening as a matched pair (amplification vs. rewriting)
- Expanded metric descriptions explaining the 10th percentile and worst-case reporting
- Added guidance on iterating with the slow AI edit

items.title: Add LLM ticket classifier with deflection analysis and ROI model
items.body:
## What?
Introduces the LLM Support Ticket Classifier — a three-component pipeline for classifying customer support tickets by category and priority, identifying deflection candidates, and modeling the ROI of automated deflection at scale.

**Files added:**
- `data/tickets.csv` — 300 synthetic fintech support tickets across 8 categories with ground truth labels
- `data/taxonomy.json` — classification taxonomy: categories, priority levels, deflectable vs. human-required rules
- `data/generate_tickets.py` — reproducible ticket generator using realistic subject/body template pools per category
- `classifier.py` — batch classification pipeline using `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`; includes `classify_single()` and accuracy reporting; saves `tickets_classified.csv`
- `roi_model.py` — ROI calculator with `calculate_roi()`, `sensitivity_analysis()`, and `print_roi_report()`
- `analysis.ipynb` — 20-cell notebook: data overview, confusion matrix, F1 by category, deflection analysis, ROI summary, 10 sample classifications
- `requirements.txt`, `PLANNING.md`
- `README.md` updated with pipeline ASCII diagram and setup instructions

## Why?
Directly mirrors the $80K+ Zendesk automation work at Tapcheck — deflecting automatable tickets from human agents to reduce cost per contact. This project packages that experience as a repeatable, quantified methodology: classify → identify deflection candidates → model the savings. Targeted at AI success and deployment roles where demonstrating LLM-to-business-value translation is the competency being evaluated, not just model familiarity.

## How?
`classifier.py` calls `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` (Haiku for batch cost efficiency over Sonnet) with a structured prompt instructing JSON output per ticket: `predicted_category`, `predicted_priority`, `deflectable`, `confidence`, and `reasoning`. The `reasoning` field is intentional — it makes deflection decisions auditable for stakeholder trust in a real deployment. `roi_model.py` takes classified output and calculates deflection_rate, monthly and annual savings, and payback period. `sensitivity_analysis()` charts savings across a 1k–20k ticket/month volume range to support business case modeling.

## Testing?
- All Python files syntax-verified
- ROI model runs standalone and output confirmed correct at multiple input scenarios
- Classifier code is fully wired but the actual API run was not completed — the build environment lacked `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`

items.title: Split chemistry tools out of server.py, and stop the planner promising accuracy it cannot deliver
items.body:
Three commits, based on current master (7cb0a35). No behaviour changes to any hardware tool.

## 1. Split server.py into server.py + tools_chemistry.py

server.py had reached 6,402 lines holding three tool sets that share no code: IBM
telemetry, IonQ tooling, and the qforge chemistry planner. Any diff touching one was
hard to review against the other two.

All three register on the same FastMCP instance, so the instance moves to mcp_app.py
and each side imports it from there. server.py imports tools_chemistry for its
registration side effect. Without that indirection tools_chemistry would have to
import server, which imports it back.

The chemistry code moves verbatim -- no logic changes.

  server.py           6,402 -> 5,738 lines
  tools_chemistry.py  683 (new)
  mcp_app.py          17 (new)

All 50 tools still register, verified via mcp.list_tools().

## 2. Fix two misleading fields in plan_quantum_chemistry_run

reaches_chemical_accuracy compared the CLASSICAL Schmidt-truncation floor against
1.0 kcal/mol and ignored hardware noise entirely. On H4 that floor sits at 0.57
kcal/mol while measured IonQ runs came back 125-135 kcal/mol off -- the flag said
"yes" where reality was two orders of magnitude away. Renamed to
classical_floor_below_chemical_accuracy, which is what it actually computes, plus a
new accuracy_assumptions field so the caveat travels with the numbers instead of
living in a docstring.

budget_usd defaulted to $10,000. Called without a budget the tool would confidently
recommend a Schmidt rank costing more than the caller's real credits. Now a required
argument -- there is no defensible default.

## 3. README

Project structure and architecture diagram updated for the new layout.

## Testing

56 passed / 40 skipped before, 58 passed / 40 skipped after. The two new tests pin
the renamed field against accuracy_floor_kcal_mol and assert the budget stays
required, so neither can silently regress.

tests/test_qforge_tools.py now imports tools_chemistry instead of server; its
assertions are untouched.

One note unrelated to this diff: tests/test_all_tools.py raises
"ValueError: IBM_QUANTUM_TOKEN is not set" at COLLECTION time, which aborts the whole
pytest run for anyone without credentials rather than skipping. I ran the suite with
--ignore on that module. Worth a module-level pytest.skip if you want contributors to
run tests unconfigured -- happy to do it in a separate PR.

items.title: feat: Add SkinGen conditional GAN augmentation for rare skin lesions (#1669)
items.body:
## Related Issue

Closes: #1669

- [x] Contributor (GSSoC)

---

## Description

Adds **SkinGen**, a conditional GAN that synthesises images of the rare HAM10000 lesion types —
and, the part that makes it worth reading, a controlled measurement of whether that synthetic
data actually helps a classifier.

Most GAN-augmentation projects stop at "the samples look plausible". This one asks the harder
question: **does synthetic data beat flips and rotations?** Classical augmentation is nearly
free, so it is the bar synthetic data has to clear.

### What was added — `SkinGen_CGAN_Skin_Cancer/`

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `data.py` | Loads HAM10000 from the `marmal88/skin_cancer` mirror (**no Kaggle credentials needed**), caps common classes, caches locally |
| `models.py` | Conditional DCGAN generator, spectrally normalised discriminator, minibatch-stddev layer, CNN classifier |
| `augment.py` | Differentiable augmentation (Zhao et al. 2020) for GAN training, plus the classical flips/rotations baseline |
| `train_cgan.py` | GAN training loop, mode-seeking regulariser, sample-diversity metric, sampling |
| `train_classifier.py` | Classifier training, multi-seed repeats, per-class metrics |
| `plots.py` | Class distribution, sample grids, loss + diversity curves, recall comparison, confusion matrices |
| `skingen.ipynb` | The whole study end to end, **with outputs committed** |
| `README.md` | Results and the full debugging story |

---

## Results

Three arms, identical architecture, epochs and seeds. Both augmented arms add the **same
number** of images (2,519 → 3,570). The test set is **real images only**. Each arm is trained
**three times with different seeds and averaged** — on a 629-image test set one seed moves
accuracy by two to three points on its own, so single-seed numbers would not be readable.

| Arm | Accuracy | Macro F1 | Mean rare-class recall |
|---|---|---|---|
| real only | **0.609** | **0.548** | 0.428 |
| real + flips | 0.553 | 0.528 | **0.633** |
| real + CGAN | 0.580 | 0.528 | 0.352 |

**Classical augmentation wins decisively on rare-class recall (0.428 → 0.633)**, paying for it
in overall accuracy — the expected trade when a model stops defaulting to the common classes.
If missing a rare cancer is the expensive error, that is the trade you want.

**The CGAN arm did not help**, landing below the do-nothing baseline. I would rather report
that with the evidence than tune until a favourable number appears.

### Why — two measurements, neither visible in the loss curves

**1. The generator had learned to ignore its noise vector.** Six samples of one class came out
nearly pixel-identical, while `d_loss` and `g_loss` sat in a textbook equilibrium. Losses
cannot see this, so `train_cgan.sample_diversity` measures it directly against the same
statistic on real images. Adding [mode-seeking regularisation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05628)
fixed it:

| | diversity, epoch 1 | epoch 300 | vs. real (0.239) |
|---|---|---|---|
| without mode seeking | 0.075 | 0.014 | 6% |
| with mode seeking | 0.224 | 0.405 | 170% |

**2. Fixing that did not improve the result** — rare-class recall actually fell (0.404 → 0.352).
Diversity was never the binding constraint. A label-fidelity check found the real cause: show
the real-only classifier 700 generated images and ask how often it agrees with the label they
were generated under.

| class | real training images | agreement | recall change vs. baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| vasc * | 109 | 0.590 | −0.04 |
| mel | 560 | 0.530 | −0.01 |
| nv | 560 | 0.400 | −0.09 |
| bcc | 390 | 0.240 | +0.12 |
| bkl | 560 | 0.130 | −0.04 |
| akiec * | 252 | 0.040 | **−0.14** |
| df * | 88 | **0.000** | **−0.05** |
| overall | | 0.276 (chance 0.143) | |

For `akiec` and `df` almost nothing the generator draws reads as that class — and those are
exactly the two classes the CGAN arm damaged most. The arm added 248 synthetic `akiec` and 412
synthetic `df` images that a classifier does not recognise as such. That is mislabelled
training data doing what mislabelled training data does.

The tidy explanation would be "too few examples", and `df` (88 images, 0.000) fits it — but
`vasc` has only 109 and scores highest at 0.590, while `bkl` has 560 and manages 0.130. The
narrower, defensible conclusion: this generator reproduced the classes whose appearance is
coarse enough to survive 32x32 and failed on the subtle textural ones.

---

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] This change requires a documentation update

---

## How Has This Been Tested?

* **The notebook was executed end to end and the outputs committed.** Every number and figure in
  the README and the PR is from that run, not an estimate. ~95 minutes on an Apple Silicon GPU
  (MPS): 80 for the 300-epoch GAN (11,700 generator updates), the rest for nine classifier
  trainings and the figures.
* **Verified 0 error cells** in the executed notebook; all 17 code cells carry outputs.
* **Fast CPU smoke run of the full notebook** (reduced epochs) before each long run, so the
  results and plotting cells were validated without waiting on training.
* **`flake8 --max-line-length=100` is clean** across all six modules.
* **The GAN configuration was chosen by measurement, not assumption** — short A/B runs compared
  a plain discriminator against spectral normalisation, tested minibatch-stddev, and swept the
  mode-seeking weight (1.0 settled at 196% of real diversity with colour artefacts, 0.3 at 143%
  and clean, hence the default).
* **Two hypotheses were tested and rejected**, which is why they are not in the code: a
  BatchNorm `eval()` sampling artefact (sampling the same generator both ways gave 0.034 vs
  0.034 — no difference), and relying on minibatch-stddev to catch the collapse.

---

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the guidelines of this project.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly wherever it was hard to understand.
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation.
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings.
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my feature works. *(the executed notebook is the verification here — happy to add a unit test module if you would like one)*
- [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules. *(n/a)*

---

### Notes for reviewers

* **This reports a negative result for the CGAN arm, deliberately.** The pipeline works, the
  comparison is controlled, and the synthetic data still did not beat flips. Tuning until the
  GAN "won" would have meant selecting on the test set. The diagnostics are the contribution.
* **`minibatch_std` is on by default but is not what fixed the collapse.** Worth knowing why it
  cannot work here: `diff_augment` randomises brightness, translation and cutout *per sample*
  before the discriminator, which inflates the batch standard deviation — so the layer meant to
  detect a collapsed batch is handed pre-randomised data. Mode-seeking regularisation works
  because it scores the generator output directly, where augmentation cannot interfere.
* **No Kaggle credentials required.** Data comes from a HuggingFace mirror and caches after the
  first run. `datasets` and `pillow` are only needed for that first download.
* **Large files are gitignored** — the image cache and the GAN checkpoint. Only the small PNG
  figures and `results.json` are committed.
* **The notebook needs a GPU** and about 95 minutes, so the notebook-health-check bot will
  (correctly) skip executing it.
* **32x32 is a deliberate compromise**, documented in the README: at 64x64 the same time budget
  gave roughly a tenth of the generator updates and never left the noise stage.
* Suggested labels: `type:feature`, `level:advanced`, `gssoc:approved`.
