items.title: Release v1.0.0
items.body:
## Release Information

- **Release Version:** v1.0.0
- **Release Date:** 2026-08-05
- **Release Type:** Major (initial release)
- **Release Branch:** `release/1.0`
- **Target Branch:** `main`

## Release Summary

The first release of `artisanpack-ui/pagespeed-insights`: Google PageSpeed
Insights testing, score history, alerting, and UI components for all three
ArtisanPack UI front-end stacks (Livewire, React, Vue), plus five artisan
commands and a CMS-framework admin-widget bridge.

This PR brings the accumulated 1.0.0 work onto `main` and carries the
pre-release review fixes in `c2b81ad`.

## Changelog

Full detail in `CHANGELOG.md` under `## [1.0.0] - 2026-08-05`. The release
workflow extracts that section verbatim as the GitHub release notes
(verified locally: 135 lines, correct bounds, no `[Unreleased]` leakage).

### Added
- Scheduled monitoring, score history, retention windows, and pruning.
- Five Livewire, five React, and five Vue components over a shared typed fetch layer.
- Authenticated JSON endpoints behind a configurable prefix and middleware stack.
- Regression, threshold, and staleness alerting with digesting and suppression.
- Five artisan commands, including a CI entry point with score budgets and four documented exit codes.
- CMS-framework admin dashboard widgets.
- Six `ap.pageSpeed.*` hooks.
- **`routes.ability`** — optional Gate ability appended to the route middleware as `can:`. Null by default.
- **`pagespeed:discover-sitemap --allow-external`**.
- **`last_dispatched_at`** on `pagespeed_urls`, with migration.

### Changed
- **Laravel 12 and 13 only.** Narrowed from `^10|^11|^12|^13`; the dev toolchain could never exercise 10 or 11, so the wider constraint was an untested claim. Deviates from the ecosystem's usual convention on purpose.
- Removed the hardcoded `version` from `composer.json`; the git tag is authoritative.
- Queue-driver failures on `POST /test` are logged in full, reported generically.
- PHPCS is now gating in CI.

### Fixed
- **`release()` no longer spends the failure budget.** Attempts are counted per *reservation*, so both release paths were burning tries and being failed before `handle()` re-ran — any cycle over ~90 jobs had its tail permanently failed by the rate limiter before reaching Google.
- **No duplicate dispatch.** During an outage every tick re-dispatched the entire due set.
- **`allow_external_urls` no longer widens result reads** — the contract the config comment and CHANGELOG both stated.
- Livewire `add()` and sitemap page entries are held to the same URL scope as the JSON endpoint.
- Child sitemaps compared on whole origin; sitemap bodies capped at 10 MB.
- Credentials redacted from stored failure messages.
- Staleness detector consults `last_tested_at`, so a short retention window stops misdiagnosing healthy URLs.
- The URL manager no longer claims deleted history that was kept.
- The digest job has a retry budget and a loud failure.

### Deprecated / Removed / Security
- None.

## Issues and Pull Requests

**Issues Fixed:**
- Closes #18

## Breaking Changes

- [x] No breaking changes
- [ ] Breaking changes documented below

Initial release, so nothing to break. Two notes for anyone tracking `release/1.0` pre-tag:

- `allow_external_urls = true` installs can no longer read back an ad hoc run against an **unmonitored** third-party URL via `GET /results/{id}`. Monitoring the URL — what an agency dashboard does anyway — restores it. This is the documented contract being enforced, not a new restriction.
- Laravel 10 and 11 are no longer declared supported.

## Testing Checklist

- [x] All automated tests passing
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [ ] Accessibility tests passing *(no automated a11y suite in this package)*
- [ ] Performance tests passing *(n/a)*
- [x] Security scan completed
- [ ] Tested in staging environment *(n/a — library)*
- [x] Database migrations tested

**Testing notes:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `./vendor/bin/pest` | 896 passed, 2190 assertions |
| `npx vitest run` | 13 files, 118 passed |
| `composer lint` (php-cs-fixer + phpcs) | clean, 0 errors across 130 files |
| `composer validate` | valid, lock in sync |
| `composer audit` / `npm audit` | 0 advisories / 0 vulnerabilities |

Manual QA against a real API key was done in the dev app (tracked outside this repo).

## Documentation Checklist

- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [x] README updated
- [x] API documentation updated
- [ ] Migration guide written *(n/a — no breaking changes)*
- [x] Release notes written *(extracted from CHANGELOG by the release workflow)*
- [ ] Wiki updated *(n/a)*

## Pre-Release Checklist

- [x] Version number updated in all necessary files
- [x] Git tag prepared: `v1.0.0`
- [x] Release branch created/updated: `release/1.0`
- [x] Dependencies updated and tested
- [x] Build artifacts generated *(n/a — JS ships as source by design)*
- [x] Deployment plan reviewed
- [x] Rollback plan prepared
- [ ] Stakeholders notified

**On version numbers:** `PageSpeedInsights::VERSION` is `1.0.0` and all 959
`@since` tags read `1.0.0`. Issue #18 asks for consistency including
`composer.json`, but that field has been **removed** — the git tag is what
Packagist reads, and a hardcoded field is the copy that goes stale after
1.0.1. A test now guards its absence.

## Deployment

**Deployment steps:**
1. Merge this PR into `main`.
2. ⚠️ **Register the package on Packagist** — see blocker below. One-time, manual.
3. Tag `v1.0.0` on the merge commit and push the tag.
4. The `Release` workflow runs the suite, verifies the tag is reachable from `main`, creates the GitHub release from the CHANGELOG section, and pings the Packagist update API.

**Rollback plan:**
1. Delete the `v1.0.0` tag and the GitHub release.
2. Nothing is consumable until the Packagist listing exists, so a rollback before step 2 leaves no trace downstream.

**Configuration changes:**
- One new optional key, `routes.ability`, defaulting to null. No existing behaviour changes.

**Environment variables:**
- `PAGESPEED_ROUTES_ABILITY` — new, optional.

## ⚠️ Release blocker: Packagist registration

The `Release` workflow is correct and matches `cms-framework`'s (it is in fact
stricter — pinned action majors, `persist-credentials: false`, and a guard
refusing to publish a tag that is not reachable from `main`). No changes were
needed to it.

But its final step calls `POST /api/update-package`, which only **updates a
package that already exists** on Packagist:

```
artisanpack-ui/cms-framework       → packagist 200  (registered, releases fine)
artisanpack-ui/pagespeed-insights  → packagist 404  (never submitted)
```

So the first tag will build the GitHub release and then **fail on the
Packagist step**. This needs a one-time manual submit at
<https://packagist.org/packages/submit> with
`https://github.com/ArtisanPack-UI/pagespeed-insights`. After that the
workflow's auto-update call works for every subsequent release.

The `PACKAGIST_USERNAME` / `PACKAGIST_API_TOKEN` secrets are not set at repo
level on any ArtisanPack package, so they are org-level — I do not have
permission to list org secrets to confirm, but `cms-framework` releases
successfully with the identical call, which is good evidence they resolve.

## Post-Release Tasks

- [ ] Tag created: `v1.0.0`
- [ ] Packagist listing live *(requires the manual submit above)*
- [ ] Release notes published
- [ ] Documentation deployed
- [ ] Announcement sent
- [ ] Monitoring verified
- [ ] Previous version support documented *(n/a — first release)*

## Notes

Three deliberate deviations from the review plan, each because following it
literally would have been wrong:

1. **Sitemap host check compares the *effective* URL after redirects.** The
   plan compared against the requested host, which breaks the deliberately
   supported apex→www redirect — there is an existing test for it.
2. **Dispatch dedup lives in its own `scopeNotInFlight()`, not inside
   `scopeDue()`.** Folding it in would silently break the documented
   equivalence between `scopeDue()` and `isDue()`, which the UI relies on.
   The dedup window is the job's own retry deadline rather than the plan's
   `timeout × tries` (~6 min), which would re-dispatch during exactly the
   outage the fix targets.
3. **Two existing tests were changed rather than the code**, because each
   encoded a wrong assumption: one asserted third-party sitemap URLs *are*
   imported (the behaviour being removed), and one described rows as "never
   tested" while the factory stamped `last_tested_at` two hours prior,
   contradicting the helper's own docblock.

P2 items 1, 2, 4, 5, and 10 from the review were left for 1.0.1 — each is a
behaviour change deserving its own consideration rather than being folded into
a release sweep. Nothing in P3 was touched.

---

- Verify all checklist items completed
- Review changelog accuracy
- Confirm version numbers correct
- Check breaking changes documented
- Approve deployment plan

items.title: feat(eval): memory-quality eval harness (LongMemEval abstention + tokens-per-retrieval)
items.body:
## What

Adds a **memory-quality eval harness** (`scripts/memory_eval/run.py`) that measures thread-keeper's *retrieval* surface — the real `search()` / `dialog_search()` / `brief()` tools — as systems-under-test, modeled on [LongMemEval](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10813) (ICLR 2025) plus mem0's 2026 [tokens-per-retrieval](https://mem0.ai/blog/ai-memory-benchmarks-in-2026) cost axis.

thread-keeper measured write *precision* (the extract-candidate ledger) but never retrieval *recall*, or whether `brief()`/`search()` surface stale or fabricated facts — so the planned lessons-decay (#27) and bi-temporal (#28) work would ship with no number to optimize against. This closes that gap.

## Reports three headline numbers over a fixed ground-truth set

- **accuracy** — per the five LongMemEval axes: information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, abstention.
- **abstention rate** — of the *never-happened* questions, the fraction correctly refused. The highest-payoff axis: it directly measures whether auto-injected `brief()` context fabricates or surfaces stale facts.
- **tokens-per-retrieval** — mean / median / max tokens of what each query returns, so recall is never read apart from cost.

```
── memory-quality eval ──────────────────────────────────
backend=fts  judge=lexical  questions=52
accuracy           : 100.0%  (52/52)
abstention rate    : 100.0%  (12/12 never-happened questions refused)
tokens/retrieval   : mean=80.6  median=42  max=271  total=4193
per-axis accuracy:
  information_extraction   100.0%  (18/18)
  multi_session_reasoning  100.0%  (8/8)
  temporal_reasoning       100.0%  (8/8)
  knowledge_update         100.0%  (6/6)
  abstention               100.0%  (12/12)
```

## Design

- **Default judge is lexical** — deterministic substring scorer (gold recall; abstention = no fabricated `trap_substring` leaks). Offline, no API key, no embeddings → reproducible and CI-safe.
- **Optional `--judge llm`** — grades answer *reasoning* (true temporal ordering, knowledge-update correctness) via the Anthropic Messages API over `urllib` (no SDK dependency); fails fast with exit 3 if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset.
- **Bundled fixture** (`scripts/memory_eval/ground_truth.json`) — a fictional "billing service" told across three sessions; a **golden baseline** where faithful retrieval scores 100%, so a regression in the retrieval tools drops the number.
- **`--db snapshot.sqlite` runs read-only** — the snapshot is copied to a throwaway temp file; the original is never opened for writing (verified: mtime unchanged).
- **Backend auto-detected** (`fts` vs `semantic`) and reported. `--semantic` opts into embeddings if installed.
- Wired as an optional `scripts/` harness, **not CI-gating** initially (per the issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A reproducible command produces accuracy / abstention / tokens-per-retrieval numbers over the ground-truth set.
- [x] The harness is documented (README "Memory-quality evaluation" + docs/ARCHITECTURE.md axis-mapping) and runs read-only against a snapshot DB.
- [x] New `scripts/` harness + small fixture set; smoke test that the runner executes (`tests/test_memory_eval.py`, 8 tests).
- [x] README section on memory-quality evaluation.

## Tests

`tests/test_memory_eval.py` — pure-function units (token estimate, lexical judge: recall hit/miss, gold_all, abstention clean vs leak) + an end-to-end subprocess smoke that asserts the three headline numbers across all five axes and that `--judge llm` without a key exits cleanly.

items.title: Rebuild the site around blue-collar and local services
items.body:
> **Stacked on #56** (which is stacked on #55). Merge in order; each retargets automatically.

## Why

The site sold to six enterprise verticals. That is precisely the generalist middle where the ~95% AI-agency failure rate lives — and it contradicted the stated intent in the workspace README of serving startups and blue-collar industries. This commits to one niche: **construction, HVAC/trades, logistics/fleet, and manufacturing**.

Niche focus is the single most consistent trait among agencies that succeed, because it is what makes components reusable and what makes a demo credible to a buyer who has been pitched before.

## One shared layout, not six near-copies

The six industry pages were ~355 lines each of near-duplicate markup. Only `manufacturing` had been migrated to the current design tokens — it literally carried a comment documenting the conversion recipe the other five never received.

Rather than copy that a further three times, this extracts `src/components/industries/IndustryPage.tsx`, driven by an `IndustryPageConfig`. Each industry is now a single server component holding metadata plus config; the per-industry `client.tsx` files are gone. Net effect: three new industries added while total industry code went **down**.

`process[].checks` is a required field on that config, deliberately. The phases read as slogans without it — "Pilot on a Live Project" says nothing, while "run in parallel with the current process, output compared against what your team produces" says something a buyer can evaluate.

## Content written for operators, not for search engines

| Industry | Solutions |
|---|---|
| Construction | Document intake (submittals, permits, RFIs, invoices), daily report assembly, bid and estimate support, compliance and safety records |
| HVAC & Trades | After-hours call capture, dispatch and scheduling, quoting from service history, follow-up and review requests |
| Logistics & Fleet | POD/BOL processing, exception triage, driver communication, claims documentation |

Manufacturing keeps its existing copy verbatim — it already fit the niche.

## Removed verticals redirect, they do not 404

The five abandoned paths may be indexed, so `next.config.mjs` gains a `redirects()` mapping each to `/industries` with `permanent: true`. Verified against a running server: all five return 308 to `/industries`.

## Two more fabrications found while retargeting

Both survived the earlier cleanup in #55:

- Manufacturing's hero visual rendered **"↓ 32% Unplanned Downtime"** and **"↑ 18% OEE Score"** — invented metrics baked into an illustration.
- `useCases.ts` carried `estimatedROI` values like **"400-800%"** and **"99.5% fraud detection accuracy"**. Retargeting those entries would have re-attributed invented numbers to the new niche, so the file was rewritten with qualitative benefits and the `estimatedROI` field dropped from the interface entirely.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` documented the old two-file pattern and listed the six old directories — it would have actively misled the next change. Updated, including a note that re-adding an enterprise vertical means revisiting the positioning decision rather than just adding a folder.

## Verification

- `type-check` clean; `lint` clean (1 pre-existing `Animations.tsx` warning)
- 29 unit + 11 integration + 16 e2e pass (e2e went 18→16 as the page list shrank)
- Build lists exactly the four industry routes and none of the removed five
- Against a running server: four industry pages 200 with real rendered content; five removed paths 308 to `/industries`; sitemap lists hub + four; process checks rendered and screenshotted

items.title: lab(needle-benchmark): Cactus Needle 26M as tool router — benchmark + verdict (REJECT as-is)
items.body:
## What

LAB-ONLY spike under `labs/needle-benchmark/`: evaluates [cactus-compute/needle](https://github.com/cactus-compute/needle) (26M single-shot function-calling model, MIT) as a fast CPU tool/intent router in front of the Gemma 4 E4B brain. Nothing is wired into the voice path, `fast_tiers`, `zoe-data`, systemd, or CI; the venv is built outside the repo (`setup.sh`), weights fetched from HF at run time.

## The four numbers (details + method in the lab README)

1. **Accuracy** (81-case corpus, Zoe's real 20-tool set, 39 paraphrase/sloppy cases): baseline Tier-0 regex + Tier-1 bge-small = **61.7% overall / 35.9% paraphrase** (generously scored). Needle full-block = **30.9%** — Zoe's tool schema is 1,924 needle-tokens vs its **1,024-token encoder cap** (8 of 21 tools silently truncated). Needle's own retrieval shortlist = **13.6%** — the released checkpoint's contrastive head emits **all-zero embeddings**. Oracle 3-tool shortlist (decoder best case) = **66.7% / 56.4% paraphrase** but only **25% on chat** (misroutes 75% of conversational turns into a tool call).
2. **Latency** (CPU, steady-state, JAX reference runtime): **p50 2.2–3.6 s, p90 3.4–4.4 s** per decision — ~50–100x the 10–50 ms target (encoder ~250 ms + ~95 ms/decode-token, no KV cache; ms-class needs the Cactus INT4 C++ runtime, not available for Jetson here).
3. **Classifier-chain cost**: Tier-0 regex 0.2 ms; Tier-1 bge-small 60 ms p50 / 82 ms p90; Tier-0.5 LLM classifier is **dead in prod** — it POSTs `/v1/completion` which llama-server 404s (always returns None after a wasted ~70 ms; would cost 1.2–1.8 s p50 if fixed). Follow-up chip spawned for that bug.
4. **Tool-prefilter value**: full 20-tool block = **1,661 Gemma tokens** vs ~**252** for a top-3 shortlist → **84.8% saved** per brain turn — real value, but achievable with the already-live bge-small router; Needle adds nothing (its prefilter head is zero-weights).

## Recommendation

**REJECT as-is.** Revisiting would need BOTH local fine-tuning AND a Cactus-runtime port. Cheaper wins captured in the README: fix/remove the dead Tier-0.5 endpoint; add missing `music`/`smart_home` domains to `semantic_router.ROUTES` (today every sloppy media/home utterance pays the 4.8 s brain lane); bge-small tool-RAG prefilter into Gemma's context.

DOX: `labs/AGENTS.md` Child DOX Index updated. `.gitignore` gains narrow exceptions for the lab's committed artifacts.

items.title: Release v1.5.0
items.body:
## Release Information

- **Release Version:** v1.5.0
- **Release Date:** 2026-08-09
- **Release Type:** Minor
- **Release Branch:** `release/1.5`
- **Target Branch:** `main`

## Release Summary

Anonymous mode is the headline: page views from visitors who have not granted consent, recorded without a visitor ID, session ID, fingerprint, IP or user agent, and surfaced in the dashboard behind an explicit toggle. On a site where most visitors ignore the consent banner, most traffic was previously invisible.

Alongside it, site resolution moves into `artisanpack-ui/core`, so every ArtisanPack UI package in an installation resolves one site from one configuration instead of each keeping its own. The JS tracker learns History API navigation, which is how Inertia, React Router, Vue Router and `wire:navigate` actually navigate — previously the tracker recorded the initial document load in an SPA and nothing else. Providers whose tracking half runs in the browser can finally contribute their snippet. And `X-Site-ID` is no longer believed by default, now that the site it names steers every package rather than only analytics.

The pre-tag review found a blocker, 8 major and 18 minor issues, all fixed in #100 — most importantly that anonymous mode could not be switched on through the served tracker at all.

## Changelog

### Added

- **Anonymous mode** — pre-consent page views to a new `analytics_anonymous_page_views` table carrying path, title, referring host, device class and timestamp, and nothing else. No cookie or `localStorage` key is created before consent. `DNT` / `Sec-GPC` still suppresses everything. (#87)
- **Anonymous traffic in the dashboard** — an *Include anonymous traffic* toggle and an *Anonymous* panel across Livewire, React and Vue, both appearing only once anonymous rows exist. Metrics that cannot include anonymous rows say so on the card. (#93)
- `AnalyticsQuery` gains an `anonymous` filter mode (`exclude` / `include` / `only`), `getAnonymousStats()`, `getReferringHosts()`, `hasAnonymousData()` and per-source anonymous queries; `GET /api/analytics/anonymous` and `GET /api/analytics/referrers`.
- **SPA navigation tracking** via the History API, behind `trackHistoryChanges` (default `true`). (#86)
- **`@analyticsScripts` renders active providers' client-side snippets** through the new `ProvidesTrackerScript` contract. (#88)
- New `tracker.track_history_changes` config key (`ANALYTICS_TRACK_HISTORY_CHANGES`), and a `config` prop on the tracker-script component for page-level overrides.

### Changed

- **Site resolution moved to `artisanpack-ui/core`.** `TenantManager` reads `SiteContext` rather than owning a resolver chain; resolvers are configured at `artisanpack.core.multi_tenant.resolvers`. A site pinned through `TenantManager` is pinned for every package, and vice versa. (#94)
- Requires `artisanpack-ui/core` `^1.3.1`.
- `TenantManager`, and `SiteSettingsService` which holds one, are bound `scoped`; `ApiKeyGuard` resolves its dependencies per call.
- Excluded-path filtering moved from `PrivacyFilter` to `TrackingService`, so a batch drops only the excluded item.
- **SPA page-view counts will rise** — that is the intent of `trackHistoryChanges`, not a regression. Apps already bridging their router must set it to `false`.
- The `country` column is gone from the anonymous table before it ever carried data.

### Deprecated

- `artisanpack.analytics.multi_tenant.enabled` / `.resolvers` in favour of the `artisanpack.core.multi_tenant` equivalents.
- `Contracts\SiteResolverInterface`, `Contracts\TenantResolverInterface`, `TenantManager::resolve( Request )`, `PrivacyFilter::isExcludedPath()` / `pathMatches()`.

### Removed

- `TenantManager::registerResolver()` and `registerResolversFromConfig()`.

### Fixed

- Anonymous mode and the SPA opt-out could not be switched on through the served tracker; the tracker route sat behind `auth`; the minified route served a feature-less stub.
- Request-driven resolvers were inert under Octane. 1.4-era custom resolvers fatalled on upgrade. ~20 call sites gated on the deprecated flag alone. `ApiKeyResolver` wrote to `sites` once per scoped query. `default_site_id` overrode another package's explicit "no site".
- Batched beacons were silently discarded by `PrivacyFilter`. (#85)
- The anonymous-table migration could not run on MySQL. (#93)
- Engagement metrics were attributed to the incoming page rather than the one measured, and accumulated across the session.
- Full detail in `CHANGELOG.md` — 30+ entries.

### Security

- **`HeaderResolver` no longer believes `X-Site-ID` by default.** Now that the resolver chain is shared, the site that header names is the site *every* package scopes by. Gated behind `ANALYTICS_TRUST_SITE_HEADER` and an optional `ANALYTICS_TRUSTED_SITE_HEADER_IPS` allowlist matched against `REMOTE_ADDR`. (#97)

## Issues and Pull Requests

**Issues Fixed:**

- Closes #85, #86, #87, #88, #93, #94, #97

**Related PRs:**

- #89, #90, #91, #92, #95, #98, #99 (the feature work)
- #100 (release-review fixes)
- [core#42](https://github.com/ArtisanPack-UI/core/pull/42) — `SiteContext::isPinned()`, released as core v1.3.1

## Breaking Changes

- [ ] No breaking changes
- [x] Breaking changes documented below

**Breaking changes:**

1. **`X-Site-ID` is no longer trusted by default.** A deployment relying on it for site selection resolves by the next resolver, or `default_site_id`, until opted in.
2. **`TenantManager::registerResolver()` / `registerResolversFromConfig()` removed.**
3. **SPA page-view counts rise** where `trackHistoryChanges` is left at its default.

**Migration guide:**

1. Set `ANALYTICS_TRUST_SITE_HEADER=true`, plus `ANALYTICS_TRUSTED_SITE_HEADER_IPS` for the gateway addresses, if you select sites by header. Tracking beacons are unaffected — they use `site_id` in the payload or `X-Analytics-Site-Id`, neither of which was ever part of site resolution.
2. Move resolvers to `artisanpack.core.multi_tenant.resolvers`. The bridge carries the deprecated list over where the shared list is empty; where it is already populated it carries nothing and logs a warning, rather than reordering resolution for every package.
3. Set `trackHistoryChanges: false` if you already bridge your router's navigation.
4. Custom resolvers written against 1.4 keep working — the bridge wraps them in `LegacySiteResolverAdapter` and logs a notice. Migrate by extending `AbstractSiteResolver`.
5. The Blade component is `<x-artisanpack-analytics::tracker-script />`. The previously documented `<x-analytics::tracker-script />` never matched the registered view namespace.

## Testing Checklist

- [x] All automated tests passing
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [x] Accessibility tests passing
- [ ] Performance tests passing (if applicable) — n/a
- [x] Security scan completed
- [ ] Tested in staging environment — n/a for a package
- [x] Database migrations tested (if applicable)

**Testing notes:**

**758 tests pass, 2 skipped, 1808 assertions** — up from 723 at review time. Green on Livewire 3.6 and 4.0. `composer lint` clean.

New regression tests were checked to fail against the pre-fix code rather than merely pass after it: the four scoped-state tests fail with the old singleton bindings, and the beacon-ordering test fails with the batch flush removed.

Verified live in the dev app rather than only under test — `GET /js/analytics.js` returns 200 unauthenticated and carries `"anonymousMode"`, `"trackHistoryChanges"` and the `Object.assign` merge form; the minified route serves the real tracker; flipping the config flags is reflected in the served body. The suite was re-run against the *published* core 1.3.1 rather than a local checkout.

Migrations: the anonymous-table migration is compiled against the real MySQL grammar in CI, added after the 191-char prefix index bug reached a release candidate because the suite runs on SQLite.

Accessibility: the anonymous dashboard surfaces were reviewed for aria-live announcements on toggle, metric labelling where a figure cannot include anonymous rows, and keyboard operability. The one change in #100 removes a Vue toggle that emitted into the void when no listener was attached, taking a non-operable control out of the tab order.

**Dependency audit:** `composer audit` findings are unchanged from 1.4.0 apart from the core bump to 1.3.1. No advisory is introduced by this release.

## Documentation Checklist

- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [ ] README updated (if needed) — not needed
- [x] API documentation updated
- [x] Migration guide written (if breaking changes)

**Documentation details:** `docs/advanced/privacy-consent.md`, `docs/advanced/multi-tenancy.md`, `docs/api/contracts.md`, `docs/api/services.md`, `docs/api.md`, `docs/faq.md`, `docs/usage/tracking-page-views.md` and `docs/advanced/multiple-providers.md` all updated. The CHANGELOG's Unreleased block was restructured to one heading per Keep-a-Changelog section, and the claims the review fixes falsified were corrected.

## Pre-Release Checklist

- [x] Git tag prepared: `v1.5.0`

## Deployment

**Deployment steps:**

1. Merge this PR into `main`.
2. Tag `v1.5.0` on `main` and push it.
3. The Release workflow runs the suite, builds the GitHub release from the `[1.5.0]` CHANGELOG section, and updates Packagist.
4. Applications upgrade with `composer update artisanpack-ui/analytics` and `php artisan migrate` for the anonymous table.

**Rollback plan:**

1. Delete the `v1.5.0` tag and its GitHub release; Packagist drops it on the next sync.
2. Applications pin back to `1.4.*`. The anonymous table is additive and can be left in place or dropped; nothing in 1.4 reads it.

**Configuration changes:**

- New: `privacy.anonymous_mode`, `tracker.track_history_changes`, `multi_tenant.trust_site_header`, `multi_tenant.trusted_site_header_ips`.
- Deprecated: `multi_tenant.enabled`, `multi_tenant.resolvers`, `multi_tenant.resolver`.

**Environment variables:**

## Notes

Two follow-ups deliberately left out of this release, both pre-existing:

items.title: Leaderboard: rank on AUROC, make both metric columns sortable
items.body:
## What this does

Two things, both on the leaderboard:

1. **AUROC is now the metric the competition is ranked on.** Balanced accuracy moves to the quieter secondary column and breaks ties.
2. **Both metric columns are sortable.** Click a header to sort by it, click again to flip the direction.

## Why the swap is small

Which metric is primary lives in two constants:

```python
# leaderboard/src/aletheia_runner/config.py
PRIMARY_METRIC = "auroc"
SECONDARY_METRIC = "balanced_accuracy"
```

The API already reported both under `primary` / `secondary`, and the page now reads its column labels, column order and cell values off that payload instead of naming the metrics itself. So swapping them again later is those two lines — no HTML to touch.

## Two things the swap forced

Balanced accuracy and AUROC don't behave identically, so `results.leaderboard()` needed adjusting:

- **AUROC can be undefined.** It's `None` when a dataset has only one label class, which never happens to balanced accuracy. The old code skipped any row whose primary metric was `None` — a fine shortcut for "nothing scored" when balanced accuracy was primary, but with AUROC primary it would have silently dropped those submissions off the board. Those rows are now kept and sort last.
- **The tie-break wasn't actually implemented.** The rules say the second metric breaks ties, but the sort only had one key. Ordering is now `(AUROC, balanced accuracy)`. This is a small ranking change beyond the swap itself — happy to drop it if you'd rather keep the ordering as-is.

## Sorting doesn't renumber the ranks

This was the one real design call. If you sort by balanced accuracy, rows reorder but **each row keeps the rank it earned on AUROC**, the ✦ leader mark stays on rank 1, and the header line adds "sorted by Bal. Accuracy".

The alternative — renumbering on whatever column you clicked — would mean the board shows a different set of standings depending on where you last clicked, which isn't what the ranks mean. Sorting is a way to read the table, not a different competition.

The ranks also have to be computed before sorting for a mechanical reason: the "show each team's best only" collapse assumes rows arrive in competition order, so the first row it sees for a team is that team's best.

## Also updated

- Per-dataset breakdown (click a row) and the Entrant's Desk table put AUROC first.
- `submit.py` prints AUROC first in the CLI results.
- `README.md` and `llms.txt` say AUROC is the ranking metric.
- `llms.txt`'s calibration section used to tell entrants the board ranks on their thresholded `deceptive` column. It now explains that `score` is what's ranked — and warns that a `score` copied straight from the binary call throws away the ordering AUROC rewards. The threshold advice is kept, since balanced accuracy is still reported and still breaks ties.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/` — 81 passed, 6 skipped (the skips are Linux-only sandbox tests, unchanged).
- Checked the new ordering against a synthetic result store: AUROC decides, balanced accuracy breaks ties, a `None` AUROC keeps its row and sorts last, and a resubmission is kept on better AUROC rather than better balanced accuracy.
- Drove the page through every sort state headlessly and rendered it in a browser against a stubbed API.

## One thing I did not fix

The ledger table is 952px wide inside an 880px sheet, so the rightmost column clips below roughly a 1050px viewport. **This is pre-existing** — it was 935px before this change, and the rightmost column was always the primary metric. My columns add 17px to it.

I tried letting long notebook names wrap, which fixes it exactly (824px, no horizontal scroll), but it breaks names mid-word at every width, so I reverted it. Worth solving properly on its own.

## Note for whoever runs the digest next

`leaderboard-top-n.js` (in the leaderboard storage folder, not this repo) picks each team's best submission by AUROC but assigns the digest's **final rank numbers** by balanced accuracy. That's why the 07-28 digest is balanced-accuracy ordered. Those published ranks now disagree with the live board — worth settling before the next run.
